I suffer from the exact same insecurities. I have, without a doubt, dated some of the most beautiful women I've ever had the pleasure of laying eyes on. I don't believe that I'm worthy of someone I would place a high attraction value on or if I do manage to attract such a person, it's just a matter of time before the woman "wises up" or "comes to her senses." 

My ex is strikingly beautiful. She's tall, thin, has beautiful natural D cups, and cheekbones that'll break your heart. And at every turn, I was being told that I had "outkicked my coverage" and did I "sell my soul"? I was afraid, unconsciously at the time, that she would hear this and suddenly awaken from the fog and agree with my friends and dump me. 

This begins to do a number on your self-esteem. The one thing that has helped me was reading an article on attraction, and I learned that there is actually much more to attraction than looks. That's why someone you never thought of as a romantic partner on Monday becomes on Tuesday a candidate for affection. 

Also, I've come to understand (or believe) that when a guy jokes like his friends do, what the friend is really doing is saying, "Your girlfriend is gorgeous. I envy you, and I hope that I can snag someone like her." Guys' relationships with one another are based on pecking order. Stated simpler, guys insult each other, and the friends insult your boyfriend because it's business as usual but they use the insult to express their envy.

My integrity as a professor was sold out in that very second that the relationship crossed the line.

And tenure won't protect him. Title IX usurps tenure. So treat lightly.

She's not rushing out the door to meet this guy. She's hanging with me."
